$comment: Document structure & validation map for StaySpot's MongoDB layer. Reverse-engineered from mongo/01_collections_and_indexes.js, mongo/02_workflow3_geonear.js and mongo/03_workflow4_facet.js. Generated because docs/mongo_schema_map.json existed only as an empty placeholder in the repo.

cross_database_relationships.engine: No FKs across engines. Postgres UUIDs are duplicated into Mongo documents as plain strings and matched by pattern, not enforced by any DB constraint.
links: PropertyReviews.booking_id -> postgres.bookings.id (optional, no format validation applied)
SearchSessions.user_id -> postgres.guests.id OR an anonymous/pre-signup identifier (schema does not restrict format, unlike property_id/guest_id in the other two collections)

PropertyAmenities.purpose: Flexible catalog document per property: general amenities plus nested house_rules / accessibility_features arrays that can mix free-text strings and structured rule objects.
PropertyAmenities.seeding_note: Populated by data_generation/mongo_seeder.py --seed-all. Generates one document per property with randomized amenities, house_rules, accessibility_features, and optional safety_features/host_guidelines.

validation.validationLevel: strict on create / moderate on collMod (see ensureCollectionWithValidator in 01_collections_and_indexes.js)

property_title.description: Optional denormalized cache of properties.title to avoid a cross-DB join on read

amenities.description: Flat list of general amenities (e.g. WiFi, AC, EV Charging)

house_rules.description: Nested array — either free-text rule strings or structured rule objects (schema intentionally left open-shaped)

accessibility_features.description: Nested array of accessibility features, same flexible string/object shape as house_rules

safety_features.description: Optional safety equipment list (smoke detector, fire extinguisher, etc.)

host_guidelines.description: Freeform object — keyless entry instructions, parking notes, host contact preferences

indexes.name: idx_amenities_property_id_unique
indexes.purpose: One amenities document per property; also the lookup path for property detail pages

indexes.name: idx_amenities_catalog
indexes.purpose: Multikey index supporting 'find properties with amenity X' style catalog filtering

PropertyReviews.purpose: One document per guest review: overall + optional sub-category ratings, free-text location tags used for review analytics, and review text.
PropertyReviews.document_count_seeded: 5000 (5 per property x 1000 properties, configurable via --reviews-per-property)
PropertyReviews.seeding_note: Populated by data_generation/mongo_seeder.py --seed-all. Generates reviews with realistic rating distributions (3-5 stars), optional sub_ratings, location_tags, and review_text. The 128-document count in performance/mongo_execution_stats.json was from a prior ad-hoc/manual dataset.

validation.validationLevel: strict on create / moderate on collMod

booking_id.description: Optional FK to postgres.bookings.id (no pattern/format check applied, unlike property_id/guest_id)

location_tags.description: Free-text descriptive tags (e.g. 'downtown', 'walkable') — the field $unwind'd in Workflow 4's most_frequent_tags facet

indexes.name: idx_reviews_property_created
indexes.purpose: Per-property review feed, most recent first

indexes.name: idx_reviews_location_tags
indexes.purpose: Multikey index over location_tags array for tag-based lookups

observed_query_behavior.workflow4_global_facet: The unfiltered Workflow 4 pipeline ($facet with no preceding $match) does a COLLSCAN, since none of the four indexes above cover 'match everything'. Per-property calls (buildReviewAnalyticsPipeline({property_id})) would use idx_reviews_property_created instead. See performance/postgres_explain_analyzes.txt and performance/mongo_execution_stats.json (workflow4_facet) for captured numbers.

SearchSessions.purpose: Ephemeral geospatial telemetry: every map pin-drop a guest makes while searching, auto-expired after 2 hours via TTL index.
SearchSessions.document_count_observed_at_query_time: ~529712 examined / 264856 matched within the workflow-3 $geoNear + created_at filter (see below) — lower than 500000 because the TTL index continuously expires sessions older than 2 hours
SearchSessions.seeding_note: The only collection actually populated by data_generation/mongo_seeder.py (target_count default 500000, weighted across 12 in-range + 4 out-of-range SF hotspots).

validation.validationLevel: strict on create / moderate on collMod

session_id.description: Unique tracking id for the pin-drop event (seeder format: sess-<12 hex chars>)

user_id.description: Guest or anonymous searcher identifier — no UUID pattern enforced here, unlike PropertyReviews.guest_id

search_radius_meters.description: Requested search radius; not set by the current seeder even though the schema allows it

filters.description: Search criteria snapshot (min_price, max_price, min_rating, required_amenities, check_in_date, guests, instant_book)

created_at.description: Pin-drop timestamp; governs the 2-hour TTL expiry

indexes.name: idx_searchsessions_location_2dsphere
indexes.confirmed_used_by: GEO_NEAR_2DSPHERE stage in the Workflow 3 winningPlan (see performance/mongo_execution_stats.json -> workflow3_geoNear)

indexes.name: idx_searchsessions_created_at_ttl_2h
indexes.purpose: TTL — background thread deletes documents ~2 hours after created_at

indexes.name: idx_searchsessions_user_time
indexes.purpose: Per-user recent-search lookups; not exercised by Workflow 3 or 4

observed_query_behavior.workflow3_geonear: $geoNear plans as FETCH -> GEO_NEAR_2DSPHERE using idx_searchsessions_location_2dsphere for the spatial bound, then applies the created_at >= cutoff filter as a post-fetch FETCH-stage filter (not index-covered). 264,856 of 529,712 examined docs matched within the 5km / 2h window in the captured run (909ms). A compound index such as {location:"2dsphere", created_at:1} is not supported by MongoDB for 2dsphere + range together in a single scan the way it is here, so this filter cost is expected, not a misconfiguration.

known_gaps_and_assumptions: PropertyAmenities and PropertyReviews validators and indexes are fully provisioned by mongo/01_collections_and_indexes.js, but no bulk seeder writes documents into them — only SearchSessions reaches the 500k+ telemetry-ping target from the assignment spec. The 128 PropertyReviews documents referenced in performance/mongo_execution_stats.json come from a small manual/ad-hoc dataset used to exercise Workflow 4, not a production-scale seed.

PropertyReviews.guest_id and property_id are UUID-pattern-validated against Postgres' UUID format; SearchSessions.user_id and PropertyAmenities have no equivalent cross-DB format check, so a malformed or orphaned reference on those fields would not be caught by MongoDB's schema validator.
